There's actually a good reason for that.

If only upvotes/downvotes count, then content with the most upvotes is the most visible. Which means most people see it and most people upvote it... it creates a positive feedback loop. Once something gets on the front page, it stays there for a very long time. That's a problem, because space on the front page is limited, and this older, already highly-upvoted content is pushing new, fresh, but less highly upvoted content down where less people will see it and therefore have a chance to upvote it.
That explains having an algorithm to drop things off the front page as they age, but it doesn't really answer the question of why you need to fudge the up/down counts to pull it off.

iirc in the post they made announcing the new vote fuzzing policy (a year and a half ago?), they said it was to discourage people just looking at what the majority voted and voting the same way. So they hide the voting break down and make it so your vote doesn't immediately show up for everyone else, to prevent brigades from immediately seeing the results of their efforts or something. The value of an upvote isn't always "1". It's "1" for the first X-many upvotes within the first Y-many hours. After that it starts to taper off. I'm guessing the scale has a somewhat logarithmic curve. Where initially your votes are worth a lot, but then they're worth decreases until they reach a point where it makes virtually no difference to the total value. Which is why you'd always see something like ~4000 as the max. This is done to improve the rate at which the front-page is "refreshed" by new content. They've also used vote-fuzzing in the past to try and make it harder to tell if you or your botnet/sockpuppet army were shadowbanned.
